full_judgment:
The said suit was decreed ex-parte vide judgment and decree dated 20.06.2007 and the property mentioned in the schedule shown in the decree of the said suit was put to execution on 04.11.2007 in Artha Execution Case No. 153 of 2007. On 22.5.2008 the said property was sold to the auction purchaser, respondent No. 10. Thereafter, the petitioner on 25.09.2008 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2008 under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Ain) for setting aside the ex-parte decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 stating, inter alia, that no notice was served upon her and the suit was decreed ex-parte and the summons was returned unserved, but no notice was published in the daily newspapers. The petitioner resided in Dhaka and on 18.09.2008 came to know about the case and enquired about the matter and on 24.09.2008 came to know about the ex-parte decree. The petitioner further stated that she is a third party mortgagor and did not enjoy the credit facility. On 06.10.2010 she submitted a pay order amounting to Tk. 5,41,523.58/ which is 10% of the decretal amount, as required by section 19(3) of the Ain. 

 I. That the petitioner executed a power of attorney in favour of respondent No. 5, Md. Saidur Rahman to execute mortgage deed. The petitioner did not authorise Md. Saidur Rahman to appear and conduct the Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 and Artha Execution Case No. 153 of 2007 on her behalf. Saidur Rahman is also a defendant-judgment debtor in Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 and Artha Execution Case No. 153 of 2007. Saidur Rahman appeared in the execution proceeding in his personal capacity as such finding of the High Court Division is erroneous and, therefore, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. 

 II. That the High Court Division committed error of law in holding that the petitioner’s application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is beyond the period of 30 days because the petitioner’s agent had knowledge regarding the suit, decree and execution case, but failed to consider that the agent is acting against the interest of the principal and as such the agent’s knowledge cannot be treated as knowledge of the principal (petitioner). 

 Mr. Shah Md. Munir Sharif, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in the light of the grounds on which leave was granted. He further submitted that the application under Section 19(1) of Ain, 2003 was summarily rejected without giving the appellant any opportunity to prove her assertion regarding date of knowledge about the decree and it is unconscionable to hold that the statement is not believable, which can only be determined through evidence and as such the impugned judgment and order is illegal and liable to be set aside. He also submitted that the High Court Division committed error of law in discharging the Rule upon consideration of so many extraneous facts, whereas for disposal of an application under section 19 of Ain, 2003 knowledge about decree is the sole consideration and the date of knowledge is a question of fact which cannot be ascertained without evidence and thus, the appellant was debarred from a chance/opportunity to prove her statements. He further submitted that the High Court Division committed error in discharging the Rule and thereby maintaining the order of rejection passed by the Adalat, whereas an application under section 19 can only be rejected summarily under section 19(5) of Ain, 2003, i.e. on the ground of non-deposit of security in violation of Section 19(3) of Ain, 2003. He lastly, submitted that the appellant executed a power of attorney in favour of respondent No. 5, Md. Saidur Rahman to execute mortgage deed and manage her property. The said attorney did not and is not in a position to depose about the knowledge of the appellant about the Artha Rin suit or the Artha execution case. Only the appellant is competent to give evidence about her own knowledge. That opportunity having not been given to the appellant, the High Court Division erred in not setting aside the order rejecting her application under section 19 of the Ain. 

 Mr. Bodroddoza, learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 10 made submissions in support of the judgment and order of the High Court Division. In addition the learned Advocate submitted that the order challenged by the writ petitioner-appellant in writ jurisdiction was an appealable order as per law and thus the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed. He further submitted that the High Court Division as well as the trial Court below rightly decided that notice was duly served as per the provision of the Ain, which is a special law and disbelieved the date of knowledge and device of the knowledge of the appellant, on the basis of the records and since the same is pure question of fact. Thus the order of the trial Court cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction and the High Court Division rightly discharged the Rule Nisi. He also submitted that the attorney of the appellant namely Mr. Saidur Rahman contested the jari case and also filed several writ petitions challenging different orders passed by the Adalat from time to time and as attorney of the appellant was fully aware about the proceedings of the suit and jari case and as such in view of section 229 of the Contract Act, 1872 the writ petition-appellant had sufficient knowledge about the same through her constituted attorney and the High Court Division rightly discharged the Rule. He submitted that the appellant did not raise any allegation or objection against Mr. Saidur Rahman for use or non-use of the power attorney in her application under section 19 of the Ain nor in the writ petition and also she did not cancel the said power of attorney till now and the unauthorized person namely Mr. Shafiqul Islam cannot be entertained by any Court of law and the High Court Division rightly discharged the Rule. The learned Advocate submitted that the property in question was sold in auction to the auction purchaser-respondent No. 10 and after full payment, the transfer deed was executed and registered in favour of the auction purchaser which has created vested rights in favour of the auction purchaser which has created vested rights in favour of the auction purchaser and as such the instant appeal does not have any merit for consideration. He further submitted that the plea of the appellant that the constituted Attorney of the appellant is acting against the interest of the appellant has absolutely no basis on record. He submitted that a proper reading of the power of attorney in favour of Mr. Saidur Rahman shows that the said power of attorney is one coupled with interest and hence irrevocable. The high Court Division after examining the impugned order rightly found that the order is passed in conformity with the evidence on record and the information available in the record of the case and as such the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order. He also submitted that the judgment-debtors in connivance with each other filed writ petitions one after another to frustrate the auction sale and the appellant claimed that on 18.09.2008 she for the first time knew about the decree, but the certified copies filed in the writ petition as annexures A to D show that applications for certified copies of those documents were filed on 7.7.2008 and requisites were put in on the same date and those were made ready on 9.7.2008 and deliveries were taken on 1.9.2008 and moreover on 11.09.2008 an affidavit was sworn with those certified copies and the auction purchaser-respondent No. 10 made a clear assertion in his affidavit-in-opposition filed in the writ petition regarding much earlier knowledge of the appellant about the suit, which was not denied by the writ petitioner-appellant by filling any affidavit-in-reply and considering the same the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed. He lastly submitted that it is clear from annexures A to D that the writ petitioner knew about the suit much earlier, though she stated in her writ petition that she initially learnt about the ex-parte decree on 18.9.2008 and on the other hand the auction purchaser-respondent clearly stated in his affidavit-in-opposition that such claim is false and the same has not been denied by the writ petitioner-appellant by filing any affidavit-in-reply and by comparing those annexures and statements it is clear that the writ-petitioner did not come before the Court with clean hand and the High Court Division rightly discharged the Rule which is not liable to be interfered with. 

 The reason given for dismissing the miscellaneous case was that the notice regarding auction had been published in the daily ‘Ittefaq’ and ‘Noyadiganta’ and hence, it was not believable that the petitioner (appellant herein) had no knowledge about the suit. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant-writ petitioner before the High Court Division submitted that in fact the respondent having published the auction notices only in the local newspapers namely ‘Doinik Somokal’ and ‘Doinik Ajker Chattogram’ which is not sufficient for service of notice in accordance with the provision of section 7(a) of the Ain. In reply the learned Advocate for the auction purchaser-respondent No. 10 had submitted before the High Court Division (and also in the concise statements filed on behalf of the respondent herein) that the required notices and summons were duly served. It was further submitted that one Saidur Rahman, constituted attorney of the appellant-Dilruba Morshed, was empowered to sell/mortgage etc. the property and therefore, the provision regarding knowledge in section 19(2) was sufficiently satisfied. 

 “It also appears that the present petitioner, Mrs. Dilruba Morshed executed a registered Special Power of Attorney on 10.10.2000 in favour of the present respondent No. 5, Alhaj Saidur Rahman, who executed a mortgage deed being No. 662 of 2006 on 05.11.2000 and also executed an irrevocable general power of attorney for selling the mortgaged property in case of default in payment of the borrowed money. It further appears from Annexure-6 of the Supplementary Affidavit-in-opposition that the present petitioner executed a Power of Attorney in favour of the present respondent No. 5 on 10.10.2000 vesting powers to act on her behalf for the purposes by the registered deed No. 5923 dated 10.10.2000 for selling, mortgaging, transferring etc. her property as mentioned in the schedule for the said Deed of Power of Attorney. On the basis of the aforesaid power of attorney Mr. Saidur Rahman executed the aforesaid mentioned deeds in favour of the Bank.” 

 In addition to the provisions regarding notice by way of publicity in the newspaper, the High Court Division also observed that an attorney of the petitioner respondent No. 5 was fully aware about the proceeding filed by the bank by way of artha rin suit and also artha jari case. The High Court Division posed the question whether in such a given fact it would not be sufficient knowledge on the part of the petitioner (appellant herein) through her constituted attorney appointed by a registered document, which is still valid? With regard to knowledge the High Court Division concluded as follows: 

 “As an attorney of the petitioner the respondent No. 5 was fully aware about the proceeding filed by the bank by way of Artha Rin Suit and also Artha Jari Case, in such a given fact, would it not be sufficient knowledge on the part of the petitioner through her constituted Attorney appointed by a registered document which is still seen to be a valid piece of document. Moreover, the publication by way of the public advertisement as to sale of the property of respondent No. 5 for himself and on behalf of the present petitioner can be taken to have sufficient knowledge of the proceedings which were going on against the respondent No. 5 to 10 and also against the present petitioner.” 

 With regard to section 19(2) of the Ain, the High Court Division observed that the petitioner would only get relief if she could show that she did not have knowledge of the ex-parte decree passed on 20.6.2007 or knowledge of the Artha Jari Case No. 153 of 2007. The High Court Division held that personal knowledge of the petitioner or knowledge through her constituted attorney would be sufficient for knowledge of the case. 

 Admittedly the appellant did not file the miscellaneous case within 30 days of the date of the decree. But the law allows her to file the same within 30 days from knowledge of the decree on payment of 10% of the decretal amount within 15 days of the filling of the miscellaneous case. This is provided in section 19(3) of the Ain which reads as follows: 

 The combined effect of sub-sections (2) (3) and (4) of section 19 of the Ain is that if a proper application is made by the defendant for setting aside an ex-parte decree in accordance with law a right accrues to the defendant to have the ex-parte decree set aside. In the present case the only point in issue is whether or not the defendant filed the application for setting aside the ex-parte decree within the time stipulated by law. Admittedly miscellaneous case was not filed within 30 days from the date of the decree, whether or not it was filed within 30 days from the date of the decree. Whether or not it was filed within 30 days from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree is a matter to be decided with the help of evidence, adduced by the parties. 

 With regard to knowledge of defendant No. 8-appellant herein, the High Court Division made certain observations which have been detailed above. It is our considered view that the view taken by the High Court Division that the appellant had knowledge through her constituted attorney is absolutely misconceived since knowledge of any party to the suit is a matter personal to that party. Knowledge can only be ascertained upon taking evidence. There is no evidence on record to indicate that even the attorney was examined to ascertain whether or not this defendant had received notices of the suit. 

 The judgment and order of the High Court Division is hereby set aside. The artha rin miscellaneous case is sent back to the Artha Rin Adalat, First Court, Chittagong, where the appellant (defendant No. 8) is to be given an opportunity to prove her knowledge as contemplated in section 19(2) of the Ain by adducing evidence. The Artha Rin Adalat is directed to dispose of the miscellaneous case within four months of receipt of this judgment.
